#9053. Atelier Zébulon Perron draws on metabolist influence for Montreal bistro

A monochrome palette and influences from Japanese metabolism characterise Bistrot à Franky in Montreal, Canada designed by local outfit Atelier Zébulon Perron.

The restaurant is a home base for local chef Francis Blais in the city’s hip Mile End neighbourhood.

Atelier Zébulon Perron took what it views as the standard design language of a Montreal bistro – bright lighting and lots of activity – and translated it into a more contemporary design.

For studio founder Zebulon Perron, the monochrome whites and beiges, interspersed with milled aluminium accents and a large zinc bar top, allowed the studio to experiment with textures and lighting to create visual interest and contrast in the dining space.

“With the monochromy of the restaurant, we experimented with textures – shiny versus matte, tile nd and stucco – and how light reacts to those surfaces in different ways,” Perron told Dezeen.

The studio emphasised the postmodern and “retrofuturist” elements of the design, pointing to the custom chandeliers with their illuminated Pyrex tubes and exposed wiring, fabricated by Perron’s long-time collaborators, local lighting design studio Lambert & Fils.

Perron highlighted the milled aluminium wine cellar that sits above the bar face, interspersed with portholes that are a direct reference to Japanese metabolist architecture.

“There’s a postmodern, 1980s aesthetic that naturally rose from everything we were doing,” said Perron.

Visitors enter the restaurant through a red-painted hallway and a metal door and handle carved from butcher block by local cabinetmaker Olivier Doray.

Inside, only the terrazzo floor was a holdover from the building’s former use. Granite tabletops cover some of the larger tables, while the classic bistrot white tablecloths are draped over the smaller tables.

Blond leather banquettes were placed below large mirrors on the wall opposite the bar, and these larger seating arrangements are centred by large butcher block tables, also fabricated by Doray.

Custom walnut chairs were designed by local industrial designer Guillaume Sasseville.

On the walls, white tile is interspersed with stucco and works of art, curated by local filmmaker Xavier Dolan. These artworks give pops of colour and Perron said that the monochromatic design elements allow both the food and the artworks to stand out in the space.

“Since the canvas is pretty neutral, the food and the artwork take centre stage,” he said.

A set of windows opens up the kitchen space to the dining room.

Custom bar seating features white columns with seats informed by transportation design, and Perron noted that the metal details and clean lines of the bar space, as well as the metal fans, also give the interior a streamlined look.

Atelier Zébulon Perron has designed some of the most interesting interior spaces in the city, including Café Constance and the dining areas for the city’s Four Seasons hotel.

It also helped create the pop-up bar staged during the city’s inaugural design week earlier this year.

#9052. Should I Exercise with a Phlegmy Cough? What You Need to Know

You’re feeling a bit under the weather, but you don’t want to lose the momentum of your fitness routine. So, should you push through and hit the gym, or is it better to rest and let your body heal? Let’s break it down!

Sleep is the best way to help your body recover quickly when you’re sick. But if you’re determined to rise and grind, you could use the “neck check” to decide whether to lace up those sneakers or stay in bed.

Many sports doctors use this theory to say that if your symptoms are above the neck — sniffles, sore throat, or a mild headache — you’re generally good to go for a light workout. But if you’re dealing with chest congestion, a hacking or juicy cough, diarrhea, a fever, or an upset stomach, it’s better to take some time to catch up on your Netflix watchlist.

Big disclaimer: there’s little scientific evidence behind the “neck check,” so use your best judgment.

If you’re going with the above-the-neck rule, exercising with the following symptoms is probably okay.

Going super hard if you have a mild cold is not a good idea. But a light workout, like a walk or a chill Peloton sesh, can be a great way to stay active without overdoing it. Stretching or light yoga might also do the trick.

Stick to light activities like walking for most earaches. Avoid intense workouts like weightlifting, yoga, or pilates, as they can throw off your balance and put pressure on your sinuses, exacerbating the pain.

Light and short workouts are likely fine if your sore throat is mild and lacks fever, cough, or swallowing issues. Remember to stay hydrated — it can ease your sore throat and is beneficial during exercise.

Light activities like brisk walks or gentle bike rides can help for allergy-related stuffy noses. If your nose is blocked, stick to very light activities, focusing on breathing. Skip workouts if you have a fever, chest congestion, or a productive cough with phlegm until you’re symptom-free.

If you’re experiencing the following symptoms, the workout can wait.

Working out with a fever increases dehydration risk and can worsen the fever. Plus, fever saps your muscle strength and coordination, making you more prone to injuries. So, do yourself a favor and skip the workout until you’re back to normal.

An occasional cough is your body’s way of clearing out irritants, but a frequent or phlegmy cough could signal a respiratory infection like a cold, flu, or even pneumonia or asthma. While a tickle-induced cough isn’t a gym deal-breaker, a persistent one is.

Diarrhea and vomiting can dehydrate you, and physical activity only makes that dehydration worse. Feeling weak? That’s a recipe for injury. Plus, stomach bugs are highly contagious. If you feel antsy, stick to light stretching or yoga at home.

The flu hits your respiratory system hard, with symptoms like fever, chills, sore throat, body aches, fatigue, headache, cough, and congestion. If you’ve got the flu, take it easy and give your body some well-earned R&R.

Once symptom-free, ease back into exercise gradually. Start with less intense workouts to avoid overdoing it. As your symptoms fade, you can gradually return to normal activity.

Regular exercise may shorten recovery time, particularly for acute respiratory infections. Listen to your body’s signals to gauge your strength. If you’re still contagious, opt for home or outdoor workouts, so you don’t spread those germs to fellow gym-goers.

#9049. Does Creatine Increase DHT? What You Need to Know

Ah, creatine! It’s a popular supplement promising muscle gains and enhanced performance. But as you’re hitting the gym harder and seeing results, there are some potential side effects to be aware of. Here’s the lowdown.

Creatine monohydrate is a naturally occurring substance found in muscle cells. It helps to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP) — your muscles’ go-to fuel when working hard.

Although you can find creatine in foods like red meat and seafood, many gym enthusiasts and athletes boost their stores with supplements. Why? Because more creatine equals more ATP, which means more energy for high-intensity activities. More fuel means more mileage!

Now, here’s where things get hairy. You might dial up your body’s DHT (dihydrotestosterone) production when you uplevel creatine. DHT is a derivative of testosterone and plays a big-league role in developing male characteristics. But here’s the catch: while DHT might beef up your alpha vibe, it’s also notorious for thinning out hairlines in peeps predisposed to male pattern baldness.

So, do creatine supplements cause baldness? Maybe! The buzz mainly stems from a small 2009 study where college-aged rugby players loaded up on creatine and saw their DHT levels increase significantly.

Because DHT can shrink hair follicles and shorten the hair growth cycle, it may seem logical to blame creatine for contributing to hair thinning. However, it’s important to remember that these findings are a one-hit wonder — they haven’t been seen again in other studies. Plus, let’s not forget that intense workouts alone can pump up these hormones, too.

As a result, the jury’s still out, making the creatine-and-baldness saga a hot topic for gym gossip and scientists alike.

The same 2009 study found that after a week of taking high-dose creatinine at 25 grams per day, DHT levels rose by 56%. When the researchers dropped the dose to 5g daily for two more weeks, levels remained 40% higher than baseline. These findings contrasted with the control group participants who took a placebo.

Does this mean creatine could spell disaster for your do? Well, creatine boosts DHT, the usual suspect in male pattern baldness, also called androgenic alopecia. However, your disposition to hair loss and the effects of DHT is genetic, meaning that it’s inherited.

Some folks are more prone to DHT’s hair-ruffling effects because of how their androgen receptor gene is wired. Hormones like testosterone and DHT bind to androgen receptors, typically triggering normal hair growth. However, variations in the AR gene make the androgens extra effective, making you more likely to experience hair loss.

So, while there isn’t much evidence to say that creatine supplements cause hair loss, the connection to increased DHT levels is worth considering if your family reunions look like a convention for bald eagles.

Beyond the potential for a breezy scalp, creatine is actually solid in the safety department, with long-term studies giving it a thumbs up. However, although creatinine doesn’t pose a risk to healthy individuals, it might not be your best move if you have kidney, high blood pressure, or liver disease.

Another thing to keep in mind is that creatinine loves to hang onto water, so expect some extra bloat and weigh-in surprises as your body adjusts.

Thinking of starting a creatine kick? Chatting with your doctor first is always wise, especially if you have other health conditions or take medications. They can advise you and rule out any potential interactions.

If you’re taking creatinine and notice changes to your hair, a check-up is a good idea. Shedding a few strands is normal, but it’s a red flag if you start losing clumps of hair. Rapid hair loss can indicate underlying health issues that go beyond your hairstyle.

Furthermore, consult a doctor if hair loss is weighing on your mind. They can offer solutions or treatments to manage your hair loss and stress.

Creatine is celebrated for its muscle-building prowess, but rumors of a link with hair loss exist. The good news is there’s little conclusive evidence directly connecting creatine supplementation to permanent hair loss.

However, creatine loading may boost DHT levels, a hormone linked to male pattern baldness, especially in people genetically predisposed to hair thinning.

So, if you’re concerned about hair loss, it might be wise to talk with a doctor before adding creatine supplements to your muscle-building routine.

AI's favourite typeface is loud, obnoxious, and everywhere.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

AI-generated art is everywhere, and not just online. If you've started noticing blatantly AI posters popping up in your own town, you aren't alone. I'm seeing the things in cafes, restaurants and even my local village hall (guys, I know you used AI to make that Fireworks Night poster). And while AI posters are generally easy to spot, there's one thing that gives it away every time: that bloody font.

You know the one. Aggressive brush strokes. A slight upward slant. It's loud, it's shouty, and it's everywhere. And now, people are comparing it to that other much-maligned font, Comic Sans. Which, if you ask me, is an insult to Comic Sans.

So why are so many small businesses happy to make posters using the exact same aesthetic? The clue might be in the name: small businesses. If you're looking for the quickest, cheapest and easiest way to produce a poster, and you haven't got the resources to hire a designer, perhaps you'll be happy to make do with one of the first things AI spits out. And if you're not as chronically online as the rest of us, perhaps you won't even realise this style is so ubiquitous.

But comparing it to Comic Sans? Come one, now. Comic Sans might not be the most serious looking typeface around, but it was handmade for a purpose. According to Carrick Signs' signage and print expert Mandy Roscoe, Comic Sans was originally created to solve a very specific communication problem, made to “mimic informal, handwritten speech in cartoons, not to decorate official notices." Mandy explains, "The problem isn’t the font itself. It’s when it’s used in the wrong context for the message being delivered.” And in 2020, it was deemed the world's second most trusted font.

As for why AI keeps pumping out the same font, well, who better to ask than AI? I asked ChatGPT, who gave me the following answer:

AI image generators frequently use this bold, brushstroke-style lettering because they've learned to associate it with exciting, attention-grabbing design. Their training includes countless posters, advertisements and YouTube thumbnails featuring oversized capitals, distressed textures and bright colours. When asked to create something dramatic, AI often reproduces these familiar visual patterns. Interestingly, it isn't necessarily selecting an actual font, but generating lettering inspired by similar styles. This reflects AI's tendency to repeat popular design clichés rather than invent something original. Ironically, typography originally intended to look handmade, rebellious and expressive has become so common in AI-generated artwork that it now looks unmistakably artificial.

So, there we have it. Thanks, ChatGPT. You're right, it does look unmistakably artificial.

#9046. Dubai Design Week's 12th edition celebrates bold Middle Eastern design

From an eye-catching exhibition spotlighting geometric forms to installations designed by prominent architects, Dubai Design Week is set to host its 12th edition to honour the Middle East’s vibrant design, craft and culture.

The programme takes place across Dubai Design District (d3), the city’s creative hub, from 3 to 8 November 2026.

The festival’s headline event is Downtown Design, an annual fair that spotlights regional and global design brands, makers and manufacturers.

Dezeen readers can get 50 per cent off their tickets using the code DESIGN50.

Taking place from 4 to 8 November,  Downtown Design presents site-specific installations, talks and networking series and exhibitions for furniture, textiles, lighting and kitchen and bathroom products.

This year, British-Nigerian designer Yinka Ilori has added his creative touch to Veuve Clicquot‘s annual lounge at the fair, which will serve as a place to relax, as well as a venue to host talks and parties.

Italian design brand Memphis Milano will also unveil an exhibition that honours the bright colours and geometric forms utilised by the group’s founder Ettore Sottsass in the 1980s, known as the Memphis movement.

Also returning to the 2026 edition is the UAE Designer Exhibition – a platform for emerging talent in the emirate within a B2B and B2C environment, creating a space for future mentorship.

Under the theme Inherited Futures, the exhibition features 30 UAE-based designers’ works, which will focus on materiality, form and technology.

With architect AlZaina Lootah as design collaborator, the exhibition tasks contributors to design products that are producible, durable, high-quality and referential to cultural contexts.

Alongside the fair, Dubai Design Week will also exhibit installations across the district, created by global architecture practices Nikken Sekkei, Sobokuya, Aestudio, Alter, Palm and Palazzo, design firm Dubai Duette Studio, architect Rasha Saffarini, cultural platform Avid Learning Middle East and craft group Dakhnii Diaries.

Programme highlights also include the annual Urban Commission competition, which will showcase the winning proposal by Dubai-based studio Nao Architects.

Titled Three Gardens and a Room, Nao Architects’ installation responds to the competition’s theme Atmospheres, which asked participants to consider “how light, temperature, sound, material and spatial design shape how we feel, move and connect”.

On display for the duration of the design week, the installation by the practice’s founder Reem Nassour reconsiders a garden with four key architectural elements – a roof, mound, hearth and enclosure – in the form of three gardens connected by a central room.

Abwab, Dubai Design Week’s flagship commissioning programme, presents In Other Words, a group exhibition open from 3 to 8 November.

The exhibition presents commissioned works by five selected practices from West, South, Southeast and East Asia, and Africa.

Its overarching theme explores communication beyond speech and writing, addressing symbols and gestures used throughout history.

Other exhibitions curated for the 2026 edition include the Worlds Ahead: 25 Years of Design, Place and Impact in the Middle East exhibition by architecture studio Woods Bagot, and the showcase by Paris’ L’école School of Jewellery Arts, which is supported by jewellery brand Van Cleef and Arpels.

Dubai Design Week’s Marketplace also returns for the latest iteration from 7 to 8 November, serving as a platform for independent makers across the Middle East.

The platform enables artisans to sell their handmade pieces, from fashion and jewellery to homeware and food, and offers a series of live performances and culinary experiences.

The festival is held under the patronage of Her Highness Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, chairperson of the Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture).

#9045. 10 Signs You Might Not Really Be in Love: How to Tell the Difference

Love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

Wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

Feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:

Caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

Chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner plans suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future plans feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

If imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love plans a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

Remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

Feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

No respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

If they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

If your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

True love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

Last medically reviewed on June 26, 2024

#9043. This week Foster + Partners unveiled the replacement for San Siro stadium

This week on Dezeen, architecture studio Foster + Partners and US studio Manica unveiled their design for Generali Stadium in Milan, which will become home to local football clubs AC Milan and Inter Milan.

The stadium will seat 71,500 people and be built alongside the 99-year-old San Siro stadium, which will eventually be torn down. Generali Stadium will be defined by a structural facade composed of elongated X-framed concrete supports.

Architect Norman Foster told Dezeen that the Generali Stadium’s design draws on his “great personal connection with the city”.

Foster also made the news this week with the launch of his first watch, which the architect designed for Spanish watch brand Lebond.

The watch draws on aviation design and was designed to be customised, in line with Foster’s philosophy that a watch is “intensely personal”.

The public vote winners for Dezeen Awards 2026 were announced this week and included Japanese studio Schemata Architects’ Uchida Shōten head office, above, in the architecture category.

We also revealed the public vote winners in the interiors and design categories. The public vote is separate from the main judging process, with the overall winners of this year’s programme set to be announced on 16 November.

In Abu Dhabi, a new concert hall by the late architect Frank Gehry was revealed. The Youth Orchestra Abu Dhabi will be located in the Mina Zayed port district.

It will be dedicated to young musicians and contain a 600-seat concert hall and 18 rehearsal rooms.

Technology brand Apple unveiled its new MacBook Pro model, which features its first-ever laptop touchscreen. The brand said the display is “a monumental step forward for the Mac”.

Apple Music also showed off a new logo this week. The first rebrand since Apple Music launched in 2015 was made in collaboration with musician Fred Again by passing sound waves through a pool of oil.

KPF completed Texas’s tallest skyscraper, a supertall tower called Waterline that is 1,025 feet tall (312 metres tall).

Its developer described the shape of the skyscraper as a “cowboy boot”. It will have hotel and office programmes at the bottom, with luxury residences at the top.

Popular projects on Dezeen this week include a pink house that brings a “fairytale flamboyance” to London, an arrow-shaped viewpoint in Denmark and a minimalist house in Japan.

Our podcast this week looked at the Oxford Street pedestrianisation and asked: what happens next?

#9042. this living garden changes color to reveal how flowers may appear to moths

studio adrien lucca explores how a garden can contain several visual worlds at once, depending on the species looking at it.

At the 2026 Ars Electronica Festival in Linz, Brussels-based artist Adrien Lucca and a team of scientists presented Parallel World, a living garden illuminated to suggest how flowers might appear to a moth. The installation brings real plants beneath a computer-controlled LED system to create a small indoor meadow that changes appearance at regular intervals. Delicate stems rise above dense foliage, with pink blossoms scattered throughout. As the lighting shifts, the garden takes on an entirely different color composition, even as every flower stays exactly where it is.

Under the bluish light, green leaves turn brown or nearly black, while the flowers become unusually bright against their surroundings. The transformation comes from the wavelengths of light reaching the plants and reflecting back toward the viewer. It is a simple visual experiment with an intriguing premise: the colors we associate with a garden are only one interpretation of what exists there. The same arrangement of plants can appear very different to another living creature.

The installation by Studio Adrien Lucca draws on the visual system of the elephant hawkmoth (Deilephila elpenor), a nocturnal pollinator capable of distinguishing colors under exceptionally dim light. While humans gradually lose their ability to perceive color after sunset, these insects can continue identifying flowers beneath the faint illumination of the night sky.

Their eyes respond to ultraviolet wavelengths alongside the blue-to-green regions of the spectrum, giving them access to visual information beyond human perception (see here). Research published in Nature in 2002 established that the species can distinguish colors under conditions comparable to dim starlight.

Lucca developed the 2026 installation with color scientist Ali Aiman Raza and researcher Colas Schretter, alongside biologist Marko Ilić, whose work focuses on insect vision. Together, they use programmable lighting to translate aspects of the moth’s visual environment into colors human visitors can experience.

The approximation has its limits, as human eyes cannot directly perceive ultraviolet light and the moth’s compound eyes process visual information differently from ours. Even so, the changing garden lends a tangible way to approach a sensory experience that would be inaccessible otherwise.

The project grew out of Lucca’s earlier experiments with plant pigmentation and artificial light. In 2022, he collaborated with Brussels-based LMNO Gallery and Belgian seed producer Ecosem to create Mondes parallèles, an installation featuring wildflowers illuminated by programmable lamps.

By adjusting the spectrum, he could change the relationships between colors within the planting, bringing certain flowers forward while others appeared to recede into the vegetation. The experiment explored how flowering plants have developed visual characteristics through their long evolutionary relationships with pollinating insects.

During a 2024 residency with Gluon in Brussels, Lucca turned his attention more specifically to the elephant hawkmoth and the colors of the night. His 2025 exhibition À l’aube du crépuscule at LMNO brought together paintings and luminous sculptures tracing the changing light of twilight.

Other works investigated the insect’s unusually wide field of vision and its sensitivity to colors humans cannot see. A drawing titled Rosetta compared the visual sensitivities of humans and hawkmoths, using visible red as a substitute for ultraviolet. The living garden extends this research into an environment where visitors can observe these differences for themselves.

Beyond the gallery, the research raises questions about the artificial lighting that shapes contemporary landscapes. Flowers have evolved colors and patterns that help communicate with pollinators, including markings visible in ultraviolet light (see here).

Their appearance depends partly on the light illuminating them, which means streetlights can alter the visual signals available to insects after dark. A 2017 study published in Nature found that nocturnal flower visits decreased by 62 percent in artificially illuminated plant communities compared with dark areas, with consequences for plant reproduction.

The effects also depend on the type of illumination. A 2021 study in Nature, using the elephant hawkmoth’s visual system as a model, examined how different artificial light sources influence the visibility of flowers against foliage.

Some lighting spectra preserved or enhanced color contrasts, while narrow-band orange lighting made floral colors more difficult for the moth to distinguish. The findings suggest that the wavelength and intensity of artificial light can change how insects navigate their surroundings, even when the environment appears perfectly legible to human eyes.

Presented in Gdańsk and later at Ars Electronica in 2026, Parallel World brings these questions into an immediate physical setting. Lucca’s work has long explored the relationship between light and perception, often through custom-built lighting systems that alter the appearance of painted surfaces or architectural spaces. Here, the same methods are applied to living plants and the animals that encounter them.

The garden becomes a way to consider how lighting design might respond to different forms of vision, especially in public landscapes where human activity overlaps with nocturnal wildlife.

programmable LED fixtures illuminate a living arrangement of wildflowers and grasses

The installation leaves open the possibility of environments designed with other species’ sensory needs in mind. Streetlights and illuminated gardens are generally developed around what people need to see, even though their light extends into habitats occupied by countless other organisms.

In Parallel World, a change in illumination is enough to reveal how much of a familiar landscape depends on the observer. The flowers remain the same, but the garden briefly offers a glimpse of another visual world existing alongside our own.

#9041. Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home.

Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up!

Why are my ears clogged?

Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked:

  • Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage.
  • If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection.
  • Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side.
  • Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too.
  • Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure.

Best clogged ear remedies

1. Pop and unclog

The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes.

2. Swallow, yawn, or chew

The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow.

3. Ear drops

Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes.

Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful.

4. Warmth and gravity

To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily.

5. Hit the steam room

Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 

6. Take allergy medication

Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears.

Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort.

7. Rinse away the gunk

Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing.

When to see your doctor

Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention.

What not to do when you have clogged ears

  • Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. 
  • Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries.
  • Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion.
  • Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation.

Takeaway

Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies.

PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

#9039. Are Tangerines Good for You? 5 Health Benefits You Might Love

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

These tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s new best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

Flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

But wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

From giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

Black Friday is still weeks away, but Bambu Lab isn’t waiting around. Its sale page is already live and runs until 1 December. And there's some serious cash to be saved on some of its most capable multicolour 3D printers.

Our top pick is the Bambu Lab P2S for $649, down from $749. For that, you'll get a fully enclosed printer with a 256 x 256 x 256mm build volume, along with an AMS 2 Pro unit that handles multicolour printing and dries your filament too.

Want something even more advanced? The X2D and H2C have both dropped in price too, and I’ve compare all three below. Meanwhile, if you want to see what discounts other brands are offering right now, check the constantly updating price widgets in our best 3D printers guide.

This fully enclosed printer comes with an AMS 2 Pro for multicolour printing and filament drying, and offers a 256 x 256 x 256mm build volume.

The H2C's hotend-swapping tech minimises purge waste. It comes with 350°C nozzles, a 65°C actively heated chamber, a 330 x 320 x 325mm build volume and an optional laser and cutting module.

All three of these bundles include an AMS 2 Pro and an enclosed printer with AI error detection, so the real question is how much multicolour work you do, and how demanding your materials are.

For most people, the P2S will be the best buy. It prints in multiple colours out of the box and handles materials such as ABS and ASA, and it’s $140 cheaper than the X2D. However, bear in mind it only has a single nozzle and lacks active chamber heating.

The X2D includes both, with essentially the same build volume, making it a smart choice if you often print with separate support material, while the 65°C chamber helps with tougher filaments. Just be aware that the auxiliary nozzle supports fewer filaments than the main one.

At the top end of the scale, in terms of both price and sophistication, is the H2C. It costs nearly three times as much as the P2S and weighs over twice as much at 32.5kg. But its hotend-swapping system slashes purge waste, and in our testing, models that’d take three days or more on an H2S took just over 24 hours on the H2C. If multicolour printing is your business, this is the one to get.

Our monthly roundup of the most popular residences featured on Dezeen captures everything from a bungalow conversion in northern England to super-luxe villas in Ibiza and Switzerland.

Read on to find out more about Dezeen readers’ favourite houses this month:

Architect Peter Morris wanted to give his “love of postmodernism a chance to reveal itself fully” with this pair of residences in north London, one inhabited by himself and his wife and another by a neighbour with similar tastes.

Bellavista 11, Spain, by Fran Silvestre Arquitectos

This luxurious villa steps down a hillside on the eastern coast of Ibiza in three low-slung volumes.

Designed by Valencian studio Fran Silvestre Arquitectos, it is unmistakably minimalist, made up of pared-back white concrete rectangles.

House on a Slope, Switzerland, by Think Architecture

An underground corridor (pictured left) connects the two parts of this house overlooking Lake Zurich, designed by Swiss studio Think Architecture.

The architects had been tasked with fitting a very large amount of floorspace onto a narrow, sloping site while being as sensitive as possible to the landscape.

Deyne Avenue extension, UK, by Loader Monteith

#9036. What's Love Got to Do With It? The Relationship Cycle Explained

Relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

Each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

From those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:

Welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

Research shows that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

Lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

If the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of new love into a warm, enduring attachment.

Hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the issues head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

Significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

If you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

You know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

Every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!

#9035. exposed concrete blocks and red tiles shape garage-turned-apartment in barcelona

in barcelona’s torre baró district, architecture studio lablanca transforms an irregular hillside garage into a guest apartment using a split-level layout adapted to the collserola topography.

LABLANCA edited by christina vergopoulou November 3, 2026 3 min

Designed by architecture studio lablanca, Llerona is the adaptive reuse of a former garage into an annex guest apartment in the Torre Baró neighborhood of Barcelona. Situated on the slopes of the Collserola mountain range, an area defined by self-built domestic architecture and steep topography, the project adapts an irregular envelope comprising a main trapezoidal volume and an adjoining, elongated double-height volume.

The interior distribution by lablanca architectural studio directly responds to two structural conditions embedded in the hillside: a raised concrete foundation block projecting above floor level and an earth-retaining rear wall recess prone to subsurface moisture. A lightweight kitchen module is mounted atop the raised foundation plinth, while the enclosed bathroom occupies the excavated recess, positioning wet programs against the subterranean boundary. This central wet core narrows the circulation path, acting as a spatial threshold dividing the public living area in the trapezoidal volume from the private, top-lit sleeping quarters within the double-height space.

To manage subterranean humidity, partitions and built-in furnishings, including the bed frame, storage units, and bathroom enclosure, are constructed from unrendered, breathable concrete masonry units. Saturated red, small-format porcelain stoneware tiles clad the kitchen plinth and the rear wall recess, articulating the structural interventions while linking the interior palette to the adjacent main residence.

The most widely cited framework for income classes comes from the Pew Research Center, which uses a straightforward formula based on the national median household income. Pew defines three tiers:

Using the most recent Census Bureau data with a national median household income of approximately $84,900, the thresholds for a three-person household look like this:

The "upper middle class" label is not an official Pew category — it is a colloquial term most commonly used to describe the band between the middle of the middle class and the beginning of the upper class. Think of it as the top quarter of the middle-income range through the entry point of the upper-income range: households earning roughly $106,000 to $169,800.

These definitions are adjusted for household size using an equivalence scale. A single person needs less income than a family of five to achieve the same standard of living. Pew adjusts all income figures to a three-person household equivalent, which is why the thresholds you see in different sources sometimes vary — they may be using different household sizes as their reference point.

National income thresholds are useful starting points, but they obscure a critical reality: the cost of living varies so dramatically across the United States that the same income places you in different classes depending on where you live. Pew Research's cost-of-living adjusted data reveals just how stark these differences are.

A household earning $150,000 in Jackson, Mississippi — where the cost of living is roughly 83% of the national average — has purchasing power equivalent to about $180,700 nationally. That same $150,000 in San Francisco, where costs run about 180% of the national average, has purchasing power equivalent to only $83,300 — technically middle class by Pew's national definitions.

This explains why so many households earning $150,000 to $200,000 in coastal cities feel middle class despite technically being upper-income by national standards. They are not wrong — their lived experience of housing costs, childcare, and taxes genuinely consumes their income at the same rate as middle-income households in lower-cost areas.

Income class and wealth class are not the same thing. The Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances reveals that high income does not automatically translate to high net worth. Many upper-income households carry large mortgages, student loans, and car payments that consume much of their earnings. Meanwhile, some middle-income households with high savings rates accumulate substantial wealth over time.

The FI community lives in this gap. A household earning $90,000 that saves 50% of their income and invests consistently will have a higher net worth within 10-15 years than a household earning $250,000 that saves 5%. Income determines your ceiling; savings rate determines your trajectory. This is why ChooseFI focuses on savings rate and investable net worth as the primary metrics of financial progress — not income class labels.

The financial independence community occupies a unique position in the income class framework. Survey data from FIRE-focused communities suggests the median household income among FI seekers is roughly $130,000 to $160,000 — placing most in the upper-middle-class to lower-upper-income range. However, successful FI stories span the entire income spectrum, from teachers earning $55,000 to tech executives earning $500,000.

What distinguishes FI community members from their income peers is not what they earn but what they keep. While the average upper-middle-class household saves 8-12% of income, FI-path households in the same income range typically save 40-60%. This results in net worth accumulation that dramatically outpaces their income class peers.

The lesson from this comparison is that income class labels describe your earning power, but they say nothing about your financial trajectory. A middle-income household on the FI path will typically surpass the net worth of upper-income households who spend freely. The FI framework redefines "class" around financial freedom rather than consumption — your class is determined not by what you can afford to buy, but by how many years of expenses your investments can cover.

Income class definitions use household income, which combines the earnings of all adults in a home. This creates a nuance worth understanding: a dual-income household where each partner earns $75,000 has the same household income ($150,000) as a single-earner household at that level, but the dual-income household often faces higher total costs (two commutes, potentially more childcare) and different tax treatment. When evaluating where you fall, always use your total household income before taxes and compare to thresholds adjusted for your household size.

The distinction between wealth and income is the foundation of financial independence. Your income class describes your present earning power. Your net worth describes your accumulated financial freedom. The FI community's central insight is that you can move from any income class to financial independence by controlling the gap between what you earn and what you spend — and investing the difference consistently in low-cost index funds over time.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Whether you are middle class, upper middle class, or upper class by any definition, your path to financial independence depends on one number: your savings rate. A middle-income household saving 50% of their income will reach FI decades before an upper-income household saving 5%. Focus on growing the gap between what you earn and what you spend — the class label takes care of itself.

Add up all pre-tax income for your household — wages, self-employment, investment income, and any other sources. Compare to the Pew thresholds adjusted for your household size. For a three-person household, middle income is $56,600 to $169,800.

Use a cost-of-living calculator to adjust your income to the national equivalent. A $120,000 income in a city with 130% cost-of-living has the same purchasing power as $92,300 nationally. This adjusted number is a more honest reflection of your class position.

Your net worth — assets minus liabilities — is a better indicator of financial health than income alone. The median net worth for upper-middle-class households is roughly $465,000. If you are above that with a lower income, you are wealthier than your income class suggests.

Divide your annual savings (including employer retirement contributions) by your gross income. The national average is under 5%. The FI community targets 40-60%. Your savings rate is the single most important predictor of when you will reach financial independence.

Multiply your annual spending by 25 to find your FI number (based on the 4% safe withdrawal rate). Then use your current savings rate and existing net worth to estimate how many years until you reach that number. This timeline matters more than any income class label.

According to Pew Research, upper-income households earn more than double the national median household income. For a three-person household in 2026, that threshold is approximately $169,800. However, this varies significantly by location — in San Francisco, you would need roughly $306,000 to have the same purchasing power as $169,800 nationally.

Upper middle class generally describes households in the top 20-30% of earners but below the top 5% — roughly $106,000 to $169,800 for a three-person household. Upper class typically refers to households above $169,800 (top 19%). The top 5% begins at roughly $280,000 and the top 1% at approximately $590,000. These are income-based definitions and do not account for net worth.

By national standards, $200,000 household income places you in the upper-income category (above the $169,800 threshold for a three-person household). However, in high-cost cities like San Francisco, New York, or Boston, $200,000 has purchasing power equivalent to roughly $111,000 to $130,000 nationally — solidly middle class in terms of lived experience.

The Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances shows the median net worth of upper-income households is approximately $805,400. The top 10% of U.S. households by net worth have $1.9 million or more, and the top 1% have $11.1 million or more. Net worth is a more meaningful measure of financial security than income because it reflects accumulated wealth, not just current earning power.

Lifestyle inflation is the primary reason. Many households increase their spending in lockstep with income increases — larger homes, newer cars, private schools, premium vacations — leaving little margin for savings. A household earning $300,000 that spends $290,000 accumulates wealth more slowly than one earning $100,000 that spends $50,000. The FI community calls this the HENRY problem: High Earner, Not Rich Yet.

Pew Research adjusts income thresholds using an equivalence scale based on household size. A single person needs roughly $56,600 to be middle income (the lower bound), while a family of five needs roughly $126,500 for the same standard of living. Larger households need more income to achieve the same class designation because they have more people sharing the resources.

Income class labels provide useful context for understanding where you stand relative to other American households, but they are a poor measure of financial health. Plenty of upper-income households are one job loss away from financial crisis because they spend everything they earn, while many middle-income households on the FI path have built net worth that places them in the top 10% of all Americans. The framework that matters most is not whether you are middle class, upper middle class, or upper class — it is whether the gap between your income and your spending is large enough to build financial independence within a timeline that matters to you. Focus on three numbers: your savings rate, your investable net worth, and your FI number. Everything else is a label that describes your present circumstances, not your financial future.

#9033. O'Sullivan Skoufoglou Architects creates "quiet yet present" garden studio in London

A low brick base anchors the timber structure of this pared-back garden studio, which London studio O’Sullivan Skoufoglou Architects created as a workspace for a creative couple in Highbury.

Nestled in a leafy garden of a Victorian home, the studio provides the filmmaker and artist with a calming, well-lit space with a strong visual connection to the outdoors.

O’Sullivan Skoufoglou Architects slotted it at the end of the garden to preserve views from the house over the mature garden, avoiding “compromising the sense of depth and continuity of the landscape”, the studio said.

“It was important that the building felt distinct from the house while sitting comfortably within its setting, a short walk from the rear garden door,” studio co-founder Amalia Skoufoglou told Dezeen.

“The intention was to create a building that felt quiet yet present in the garden, rather than competing with it or the Victorian house,” she added.

“The form allows the quality of the space to emerge through its proportions, construction and relationship with daylight,” Skoufoglou continued. “Its modest scale and subservient position give the studio the character of a garden building.”

O’Sullivan Skoufoglou Architects designed the material palette and low profile of the studio to complement the character of the existing house and garden, ensuring minimal visual impact.

Its low brick plinth nods to the brick boundary walls of the Victorian home and also pays homage to Victorian glasshouses, traditionally supported on low brick walls.

Above the brick plinth is a lightweight timber structure, chosen to “allow the upper part of the building to remain visually light”, Skoufoglou said.

Inside, the garden studio comprises a main open workspace and an adjoining bathroom. The focal point is its built-in desk that extends along the main east-facing window wall.

“The main window wall and the built-in desk form the focus of the interior. The desk runs alongside the generous east-facing windows, making daylight and the changing garden views an integral part of the working environment,” said Skoufoglou.

“This arrangement brings the working surface into direct relationship with natural light and views of the garden.”

Inside, the timber structure is left exposed at roof level, while the brick plinth is also left visible. Between, the walls are lined with painted pine.

According to the studio, the “grain of the timber, the texture of the brick and the changing daylight combine to give the space its character”.

Other London garden studios featured on Dezeen include Shou Sugi Bangers, a timber music studio by Unknown Works, and Gardenhide Studio, a hempcrete workspace by Commonbond Architects.

#9032. Vibration Plate Benefits, According to a Weightlifting Coach

Vibration plates are like mini surfboards that give you a good shimmy while you’re exercising. Though you won’t find a mountain of extensive research behind them, you may be impressed by their possible benefits.

We asked a weightlifting coach to explain and show us how to add good vibrations to our workout routine.

These machines, which look like platforms or scales, are designed to activate something called whole-body vibration (WBV). WBV makes the body work harder by forcing it to contract muscles automatically.

Fans of WBV like to perform classic exercises on top of these machines, including:

Research points to WBV’s ability to boost blood flow.

Weightlifting coach Jarrod Nobbe explains that vibration plates help move blood by stimulating muscle contractions through rapid vibrations.

“The rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles help pump blood more efficiently throughout the body,” he says.

As Nobbe adds, movement generally increases blood flow and core temperature, preparing the body for activity. This means vibration plates may be an excellent warm-up activity.

A 2021 study showed that WBV can be an alternative exercise for older adults, boosting the effects of strengthening exercise.

Nobbe says this is because WBV engages muscles in a way that mimics resistance training.

“The vibrations activate and force muscles to contract and relax multiple times per second, which can lead to gains in muscle strength and endurance over time, especially when combined with specific exercises,” he says.

Nobbe points to some anecdotal evidence suggesting that regular use of vibration plates may help boost energy levels, possibly thanks to increased blood circulation and enhanced muscle activation.

“Ultimately, I stand by the idea that movement is medicine,” Nobbe says. “Tons of research already proves that regular physical activity boosts mood, mental health, and promotes energy levels.”

Nobbe says WBV may reduce muscle soreness, stiffness, and inflammation by encouraging blood flow to the muscles. This, he explains, aids in faster recovery post-exercise or injury.

WBV has been shown to improve bone mineral density, which Nobbe points out may positively affect those at risk of osteoporosis.

“The mechanical vibrations stimulate bone cells, potentially leading to increased bone density and strength, delivering the same positive bone health benefits of resistance training,” he says.

“Unfortunately, vibration plates aren’t a one-stop shop for weight loss,” Nobbe says.

He explains that vibration plates alone are unlikely to significantly reduce belly fat without dietary changes and additional exercise.

“While vibration plates can contribute to overall calorie expenditure and muscle activation, targeted fat loss requires a comprehensive approach including diet, cardio exercise, and resistance training,” he says.

These tips will help you stand on your vibration plate with a slight bend at your knee or perform exercises on top of it.

More research is needed around WBV — AKA what happens when you use a vibration plate — but existing smaller research is promising.

Use your machine carefully, and remember to maintain a healthy lifestyle and workout routine.

Last medically reviewed on June 27, 2024

#9031. Em-Estudio lines Mexico City bar with walls of books

Photography by Nin Solis (unless stated otherwise)

The vintage bookstores of Mexico City‘s Roma neighbourhood influenced the interiors of this basement bar, designed by local outfit Em-Estudio.

Located below an early 20th-century house in the Mexican capital’s historic colonia, Libreria Valladolid was designed to evoke the experience of exploring old bookshops.

“It captures the thrill felt when entering these places, searching for a unique story that has patiently waited among thousands of books on all topics and from many eras,” said Em-Estudio.

Accessed from the street through an unassuming door, the entry vestibule features shelves packed with old volumes and more stacks along a wooden staircase that descends to another threshold.

Small lamps are squeezed between the spines and placed on top of the stacks, creating a moody glow that sets the scene for the bar beyond.

“The old bookstore is encountered upon entering, as you descend the stairs, and it remains behind as you cross the first threshold, where the books transform into the skin that embraces the rooms,” said the studio.

Inside the basement, dark herringbone flooring and surfaces drenched in burgundy continue the bookshop atmosphere.

The larger walls are lined entirely with shelves filled with books stacked spine inwards, so the warm beige of their pages faces the room.

Cove lighting illuminates the books, creating a dramatic contrast with the otherwise shadowy bar, while banquettes below are accompanied by circular marble tables for placing drinks.

“The pages of thousands of books resting on bookshelves that reach the ceiling shed their literal meaning, becoming a tapestry in shades of white that only time can give, bathed in a gradient of warm light,” Em-Estudio said.

Other areas such as the DJ booth, the bar and the bathrooms are highlighted with gold leaf and brass to draw the eye.

A further hidden lounge space is disguised by another bookshelf, decorated with cans and objects that “evoke a grocery-store bar”.

This room swaps burgundy for green, applied in gloss across the ceiling and appearing in a long marble table that runs through the centre.

Dark wood Van Beuren chairs with yellow upholstery are lined up along each side, parallel to more walls of books that are uplit along each shelf.

A mirror that covers the back wall visually doubles the space, extending the table and the bookshelves in the reflection.

Em-Estudio was co-founded by architect Ivan Esqueda and interior designer Gala Sánchez-Renero – a husband and wife who also operate individual practices.

Their previous collaborations include a holiday home on a steep hillside in Oaxaca, Mexico, built from coloured concrete chosen to blend into the rocky mountainside.

Architecture and interior design: Taller Ivan Esqueda and Gala Sánchez-Renero Estudio Design team: Berenice Galindo, Sergio Peláez, Fabián CedilloConstruction and installations: Miguel Ángel MárquezCarpentry: Leonardo Cabrera

#9030. misha kahn turns upholstery into painting and marble into fabric at friedman benda

the designer discusses his return to hands-on experimentation, where unexpected materials and processes reshape familiar domestic objects.

Misha Kahn‘s latest exhibition, All Intensive Purposes, brings a radical collection of furniture and sculpture to Friedman Benda, marking ten years of collaboration with the gallery. A sofa resembles a pile of painted shapes, and a marble console seems to sag beneath the drapes of its own fabric-like surface.

The works reveal Kahn’s fascination with material experimentation and the unpredictable ways an idea can develop through the process of making. At the show’s opening, designboom spoke with the artist and designer about the thinking behind these unusual objects and his return to more tactile methods of working.

Throughout the New York gallery, familiar objects take on unexpected qualities. Striped plywood returns to tree-like forms, copper is worked into the appearance of loosely knitted fabric. There’s even a ‘lazy river’ circulating through the space.

For much of his career, Misha Kahn has moved between physical craft and digital experimentation, producing furniture through everything from improvised molds to virtual reality. His earlier work often carried the exaggerated, gravity-defying appearance of objects conceived on a computer screen. This time, he describes a shift toward something more immediate.

‘I think, the past handful of years, I really was doing so much work conceptually, digitally,‘ the artist tells designboom. ‘I think this show was really sort of a studio move.‘ Working partly from his studio in the woods, he describes a spiritual shift toward something ‘really tactile,’ with collage and material experimentation becoming central to the new pieces.

The new upholstered pieces offer one of the clearest examples of Kahn’s current approach. Their rounded forms appear assembled from enormous painted fragments, with irregular cushions that overlap and separate. Kahn explains that the process began with a painted composition, which was subsequently translated into wool by textile studio JG SWITZER. The material was then brought back into the furniture-making process, with patterns used to reconstruct the original painted arrangement across the upholstered surfaces.

‘I’ve never gotten that control over the surface,‘ the artist says, explaining that conventional upholstery typically requires working within the limitations of existing fabrics. The new process allowed him to develop the form and its graphic treatment together.

The construction underneath is equally unconventional. ‘We make the frames in the studio, and they’re welded so that the shapes can really flow,‘ Kahn explains. ‘I find that the most satisfying part is sort of the air between the cushions, because we’re so used to seeing a continuous form.‘ Some of the cushions appear loosely attached, raising questions about which parts can actually be moved, while additional pillow elements extend the composition even further.

Perhaps the exhibition’s most unexpected addition is a miniature lazy river, a winding installation that circulates through the gallery alongside a large video projection. The idea came to Kahn with surprising simplicity. ‘I thought, I don’t know why, I think like the beach,‘ he recalls, laughing. ‘I was like, this show needs a lazy river.‘

The video presents an abstract sequence of actions in which materials are repeatedly manipulated and transformed, eventually producing a kind of juice. ‘I wanted to make this video, like, a really abstract version of what it feels like to make objects,‘ he explains, describing the experience of doing something, taking it apart, and putting it back together over and over again.

Kahn designed a series of plastic bottles to accompany the installation, using the familiar manufacturing process associated with commercial water bottles to produce unusual, doubled forms. The arrangement circles continuously, offering a physical interpretation of the exhibition’s title, All Intensive Purposes, which shifts the familiar expression toward the intensity of making, even when the destination remains uncertain.

Kahn has spent much of his career working somewhere between furniture and sculpture. His pieces maintain a recognizable connection to domestic objects, while their unusual proportions and complex surfaces complicate their intended use. In Throws of Passion, for instance, a substantial marble console is carved to resemble draped fabric, its folds appearing almost weightless despite the solidity of the stone.

Asked whether his practice has recently moved further toward sculpture or functional furniture, Kahn describes both as part of the same imagined environment. ‘I feel like I always just wanted to feel like it’s coming from one world,‘ he says. ‘Objects really communicate an idea because I think you understand them as, like, oh, this is what’s in the house, and this is what goes there.‘

He also acknowledges the freedom that comes with making objects beyond the expectations of furniture. ‘I have really enjoyed making sculpture because it just doesn’t have some of the same kind of requirements,‘ he explains. Still, the distinction appears of limited interest to him. ‘I always feel like it should have both. All of my favorite historical figures did both.‘

#9029. Toot Toot! 6 Tips to Prevent Protein Farts

Protein farts are a common, albeit smelly, side effect of high-protein diets. They happen because of how proteins are digested. But(t) don’t worry! We have some tips to help you say goodbye to those pungent protein toots without giving up your gains.

Protein farts are episodes of flatulence that don’t smell too pleasant! They’re generally due to upping your protein intake from supplements like protein shakes.

And while these butt whistles may be embarrassing, you’ll be glad to know they’re generally harmless.

Farts consist of different gases. The most stinky odors usually come from your gut bacteria, producing sulfur-containing compounds as they break down food. The main culprit is hydrogen sulfide, which gives off a characteristic rotten egg smell, yum!

But why do your protein choices lead to thunder from down under?

Well, there’s not much evidence that a high-protein diet causes protein farts. However, there’s some anecdotal evidence that supplementary protein — like protein bars, protein shakes, and powder powders — increases flatulence, but it’s likely due to non-protein ingredients like lactose.

Supplements containing whey protein or casein are derived from milk and are high in lactose, which can increase flatulence. If your body can’t properly digest lactose, it ends up in your colon, where bacteria feast on it, producing — you guessed it — more gas and cheek flapping.

So, whey protein can throw a curveball for those who are lactose intolerant or sensitive. Surprisingly, it might also stir up digestive drama even for folks who typically handle dairy like champs, potentially due to additives like fart-inducing sweeteners or thickeners.

Some people may also have more significant issues digesting protein. Proteins are big, complex molecules — breaking them down is no small task for your gut. Plant-based protein supplements, like those based on soya beans, may also worsen flatulence.

FYI: Another reason why flatulence is common with protein powders and supplements is due to the addition of artificial sweeteners in the powders and bars, like sugar alcohols, sucralose, sorbitol, xylitol, and stevia.

If you’re looking to continue your protein regimen without becoming a walking, talking whoopee cushion, here are some strategic adjustments you can make:

Don’t just dive into the deep end with your protein intake — wade in slowly. Gradually increasing the amount of protein you consume allows your digestive system to adjust without getting overwhelmed. This step-by-step approach can help minimize the likelihood of excessive gas.

Keep the water flowing. Drinking plenty of water is crucial as it helps your digestive system handle higher protein levels more efficiently. Proper hydration aids in the breakdown and absorption of nutrients, which can help prevent gas buildup.

Sometimes, your body needs a little extra help. Enzyme supplements like Beano or Lactaid can be game-changers, especially if you consume proteins that your body struggles with. These supplements help break down proteins and lactose, making digestion smoother and less gassy.

Variety isn’t just the spice of life — it can also be the solution to your protein fart problems. If whey protein tends to upset your stomach, explore other options like plant-based or animal-based proteins that might be easier to digest. Diversifying your protein sources can also ensure you get a broad range of nutrients.

What you blend your protein powder with can make a big difference. If you’re whipping up a protein shake, be mindful of adding high-fiber fruits and vegetables, as these can also increase gas production. Try to find a balance that allows you to enjoy the benefits of protein and fiber without the extra flatulence.

Introducing probiotics into your diet can improve your gut health, which can help manage and reduce gas production. Whether through supplements or probiotic-rich foods like yogurt, kefir, or sauerkraut, boosting your gut flora can aid in better overall digestion and less discomfort from gas.

Protein farts are a rather windy side effect of a high-protein diet, but they don’t have to knock you off course. Try easing into your protein consumption, staying hydrated, diversifying your protein sources, and integrating enzyme supplements or probiotics to max those gains, minus the stink bombs!
